name: Sermorelin

lead: Sermorelin is a synthetic fragment of growth hormone releasing hormone consisting of its first 29 amino acids. It was FDA-approved for diagnosing and treating growth hormone deficiency in children before manufacturing ceased in 2008.

It is still available through compounding pharmacies and used off-label for age-related decline. Its hormonal mechanism is documented, while evidence for visible body-composition or cosmetic benefit is limited.

paras: It acts on GHRH receptors in the pituitary to prompt natural, pulsatile growth hormone release, so the body's feedback mechanisms still operate, unlike with injected GH.

It is prescription-only in the US and banned in competitive sport. Common effects are injection-site reactions, flushing and headache. It is avoided with active cancer and in pregnancy. Quality of compounded preparations and the claims made in telehealth marketing are reported to vary.
